summary: Two added catch blocks drop export failures
explanation: The pull request adds a retry around the invoice export. Two of its new catch blocks end the failure path without logging, rethrowing or recording the failed export, so an operator cannot tell a dropped invoice from a sent one. A third catch in the same change keeps the invoice id and rethrows, which is the shape the criteria ask for.

problems.summary: Timeout during export is caught and ignored
problems.explanation: The added catch block discards the TimeoutException. The export then returns normally, so the caller records the invoice as sent although the gateway never received it.

basis.explanation: The change widens the swallowed exception from IOException to Exception.

problems.nextStep: Log the timeout with the invoice id and rethrow it, or record the invoice as a failed export so that the retry policy sees it.

problems.summary: Retry failure is logged only at debug level
problems.explanation: The retry policy logs the final failure at debug level and then returns false. Production runs at info level, so the failure leaves no trace.

basis.explanation: This pull request adds the debug-level log call on the new side of the change.

problems.nextStep: Log the final retry failure at warn level with the invoice id.

example.note: This catch keeps the invoice id and rethrows the cause. The two catches above can follow the same shape.

search.lookedFor: catch blocks and error callbacks that this pull request adds or changes and that drop the error
search.boundary: every hunk of the three changed files; unchanged code only where a changed line calls it

openQuestions.openQuestion: Is an empty result here the documented contract for a missing invoice, or does it hide a failed lookup?
openQuestions.wouldSettleIt: The contract of InvoiceRepository.findForExport, or a caller that treats an empty result as an error.

omitted.what: lines of the export client beyond the read limit
